Only those saints in-drink this nectar and bathe their mind in it, who have served their Lord in the past.
Those people who served the True Guru and the saints in past births bathe in this pool of amrit and drink it with their minds attached.
L446: Tin = their (the saints'). Nivar = removing. Anbhai pad = the state of fearlessness. Sabad matr = just by reciting his Word. Udhar dhare = has delivered, has carried across.
(Guru Ramdas ji) has removed the fear of those (saints) and blessed them with the state of fearlessness, and just by reciting his Word he has carried them across.
God takes their fears away, and blesses them with the state of fearless dignity. Through the Word of His Shabad, He has saved them.
The Lord drives away their fear, blesses them with the fearless status and ferries them across through His name alone.
You have removed those people's fear of birth and death and given the fearless state, which is the form of direct experience; you have delivered them by teaching alone.
8QVX: O poet Kalyasahar! Guru Ramdas ji, the son of Thakur Hardas ji, fills the empty pools (of hearts with the amrit of the Name). ||2||
So speaks KALL the poet: Guru Raam Daas, the son of Har Daas, fills the empty pools to overflowing. ||2||
Says Kalsahar, the bard, Guru Ram Dass, the son of the Thakar Har Dass, fills the empty tanks.

Sri 'Kal' the poet says: O Sri Guru Ramdas Sahib ji, son (tanai) of Hardas ji, the chief (thakur) or master! Those whose heart-pools were empty of love, you have filled with virtues such as love. ||2||
GWL3: Satgur mat = the True Guru's understanding. Goorh = deep. Bimal = pure. Atam = the soul. Rang = in the love (of Hari). Chalool = deep-dyed. Bhaya = has become.
The Guru's (Ramdas ji's) understanding is deep, (his) company of the true is pure; (and his) soul is deeply dyed in Hari's love.
The True Guru's understanding is deep and profound. The Sat Sangat is His Pure Congregation. His Soul is drenched in the deep crimson color of the Lord's Love.
Profound is the True Guru's understanding, his association makes man blotless and his soul is imbued deep red with the love of his Lord.
O True Guru ji! Your understanding (mat) is very deep and your company of the true is also supremely pure, because you have attained the bliss of the self, very deep (chalool), that is, dense.
XX7Q: Sahaj = in the state of poise, through spiritual steadiness. Prakasya = has blossomed. Abhai = fearless. Gharahi = in the very home (of the heart). Laha = has been found.
(True Guru Ramdas ji's) mind is awake, the lotus (of his heart) has blossomed in spiritual poise, and (he) has found the fearless Hari within his own heart.
The Lotus of His mind remains awake and aware, illuminated with intuitive wisdom. In His own home, He has obtained the Fearless, Immaculate Lord.
Illumined with Divine knowledge, his mind lotus remains awake and in his very home he has attained the fear-free immaculate Lord.
When the sun of wisdom (sahaj) shone in your mind, the lotus of your mind (awoke) blossomed, and so you found the fearless Pure One in the home of the heart.

63TS: Satgur dayal = the compassionate Guru (Amardas ji). Drirhaya = has firmly implanted (in Guru Ramdas ji). Tis prasad = by the grace of that (Name). Panch = the five (vices) such as lust. Vas kare = (Guru Ramdas ji) has brought under control.

The compassionate Guru (Amardas ji) firmly implanted the Name (in Guru Ramdas ji) (that is, had him chant it); by the blessing of that Name (Guru Ramdas ji) has brought the five, such as lust, under his control.
The Merciful True Guru has implanted the Lord's Name within me, and by His Grace, I have overpowered the five thieves.
The merciful True Guru has implanted the Lord's Name within me and by his grace, I have disciplined the five demons.

Because Sri Satguru Amardas Sahib ji, being compassionate, implanted Hari's Name in you, by his grace you have brought the five enemies, lust, anger and the rest, under your control, that is, made them subject to you.
0QJY: O poet Kalyasahar! Guru Ramdas ji, the son of Thakur Hardas ji, fills the empty pools (of hearts with the amrit of the Name). ||3||
So speaks KALL the poet: Guru Raam Daas, the son of Har Daas, fills the empty pools to overflowing. ||3||
Says Kalsahar, the bard, Guru Ram Dass, the son of Thakar Har Dass, fills the empty tanks.

Sri 'Kal' the poet says: O Sri Guru Ramdas Sahib ji, son (tanai) of Hardas ji, the chief (thakur) or master! Those whose heart-pools were empty of love, you have filled with virtues such as love. ||3||
R4W8: Anbhau = wisdom (anubhav, direct experience). Unman = through inference, through reflection. Akal = (akal: 'that which has no parts'; not in parts, without parts, an epithet of the Supreme Spirit) Hari, pervading all evenly. Paras = (Guru Amardas ji). Bhetia = met. Sahaj ghare = in the home of peace.

(Guru Ramdas ji) gained wisdom through reflection; (his) attention is joined to Hari, who pervades all evenly. (Guru Ramdas ji) met the philosopher's stone (Guru Amardas), (by whose blessing Guru Ramdas) has reached the state of poise.
With intuitive detachment, He is lovingly attuned to the Fearless, Unmanifest Lord; He met with Guru Amar Daas, the Philosopher's Stone, within his own home.
With detached mind, the Guru is attuned to the fearless and Inconceivable Lord and has met with God, the philosopher's stone, in his very home.

By reflecting (unman) on the Form of direct experience, your attention is fixed on the Supreme Self, who is free of strife (akal), and Satguru Amardas Sahib ji, the philosopher's stone, met you naturally (sahaj) at home.
0UFD: Parsad = by the grace. Bhagat bhai = with the love of devotion. Bhandar = treasures.
By the grace of the True Guru (Amardas ji), (Guru Ramdas) has attained the highest state, and (his) treasures are full with the love of devotion.
By the Grace of the True Guru, He attained the supreme status; He is overflowing with the treasures of loving devotion.
By The True Guru's grace, he has obtained the supreme status and his treasures are brimful with meditation and love.
So by the grace of that True Guru you have attained the state of liberation, and so your storehouses are full of devotion and love.
GJKQ: Janmant = birth and end, birth and death. Maran bhau = the fear of death. Santokh sare = in the pool of contentment, in the Timeless Being.
Guru Ramdas ji has erased (his) birth and death; (his) fear of death has gone, and (his) mind is joined to the Timeless Being, the pool of contentment.
He was released from reincarnation, and the fear of death was taken away. His consciousness is attached to the Lord, the Ocean of contentment.
He is rid of future births, his fear of death is removed and his mind is attached to God, the ocean of contentment.
You have erased birth, and the fear of death at the end has also fled. Your mind is attached to the Supreme Lord, the ocean of virtues such as contentment.
UNSM: O poet Kalyasahar! Guru Ramdas ji, the son of Thakur Hardas ji, fills the empty pools (of hearts with the amrit of the Name). ||4||
So speaks KALL the poet: Guru Raam Daas, the son of Har Daas, fills the empty pools to overflowing. ||4||
Says Kalsahar, the bard, Guru Ram Dass, the son of 'Thakar Har Dass, fills the empty tanks.

Sri 'Kal' the poet says: O Sri Guru Ramdas Sahib ji, worthy son of Sri Haridas, the master (thakur)! The pools that were empty, meaning the poorest of the poor, you have in your grace filled with every kind of wealth, or with virtues. ||4||
CB6J: Abhar bhare = the one who fills the unfilled, Hari who fills empty hearts. Payau = has attained. Apar = the infinite Hari. Rid antar = in the heart. Dhario = has enshrined.
(Guru Ramdas ji) has found the infinite Hari, who fills empty hearts; (he has) enshrined (the infinite Hari in his) heart,
He fills the empty to overflowing; He has enshrined the Infinite within His heart.
The empty ones you fill, O Guru. You have obtained the infinite Lord whom you have enshrined in your mind.
O True Guru ji! You have filled the empty (abhar), you have meditated on the infinite Vahiguru, and in your heart you have held the meditation of him alone.
QQHG: Tat = the source of all creation. Atam prabodh = Hari, who awakens the soul. Beecharo = has remembered.
(And in his) mind he has remembered (that) Timeless Being (who) destroys pains and awakens the soul.
Within His mind, He contemplates the essence of reality, the Destroyer of pain, the Enlightener of the soul.
Within your mind you reflects on the 'Real thing, who is the Destroyer of distress and the awakener of the soul.
In the hearts of those who hold the meditation, the knowledge of the self that destroys pains has arisen, and they have reflected well in their minds on what is real and what is false.
PRR9: Chai = in eagerness, in joy. Har bhai = in Hari's love. Janai = knows.
(Guru Ramdas) is always in joy, (absorbed) in Hari's love, (and) he alone knows the taste of (Hari's) love.
He yearns for the Lord's Love forever; He Himself knows the sublime essence of this Love.
You ever yearn for the Lord's love and yourself realise the relish of this love.
You always have eagerness (chai) for Hari's love (bhai); you alone know the taste of that love.
9FG5: Satgur kai parsad = by the grace of the Guru (Amardas ji). Manai = enjoys. Sahaj setee = with spiritual poise.
By the grace of the True Guru (Amardas ji), (Guru Ramdas) enjoys bliss in spiritual poise.
By the Grace of the True Guru, He intuitively enjoys this Love.
By the True Guru's grace, you enjoy celestial beatitude with ease.
By the grace of the True Guru, the third Patshah ji, you are enjoying (manai) bliss (rang) together with wisdom (sahaj).
NXJV: Nanak prasad = by the grace of (Guru) Nanak. Angad sumat = with the good understanding given by (Guru) Angad (Dev ji). Gur amar = Guru Amardas. Amar = the command (of the Timeless Being). Vartaio = has practised, has put into practice.
By the grace of (Guru) Nanak ji (and) with the fine understanding given by (Guru) Angad ji, Guru Amardas ji put the command of the Timeless Being into practice,
By the Grace of Guru Nanak, and the sublime teachings of Guru Angad, Guru Amar Daas broadcast the Lord's Command.
Through the grace of Nanak and the sublime instruction of Angad Guru Amar Dass brought into play the Lord's command.
By the grace of Sri Guru Nanak Sahib ji, Sri Guru Angad Sahib ji received excellent understanding (sumat). After that, he made Sri Guru Amardas Sahib's command (amar) prevail.
JP4V: Gur Ramdas = O Guru Ramdas! Kalyuchrai = Kal uchrai, Kalyasahar says. ||5||
The poet Kalyasahar says, O Guru Ramdas ji! You have attained the state of the eternal, imperishable Hari. ||5||
So speaks KALL: O Guru Raam Daas, You have attained the status of eternal and imperishable dignity. ||5||
Says Kall, the bard, you, O Guru Ram Dass, has attained the eternal and imperishable dignity.
Sri Kal ji utters: O Sri Guru Ramdas Sahib ji! By the grace of Sri Guru Amar Das Sahib ji you have attained the unshakable, immortal state. ||5||
AMQP: Sarovar = in the pool. Basai = (Guru Ramdas) dwells. Amia ras = the taste of the amrit of the Name. Rasan = with the tongue. Prakasai = makes manifest.
(Guru Ramdas) dwells in the pool of contentment, (and with his) tongue makes manifest the taste of the amrit of the Name.
You abide in the pool of contentment; Your tongue reveals the Ambrosial Essence.
You abide in the tank of contentment and your tongue reveals the delicious Name-Nectar.
O True Guru ji! You dwell in the pool of virtues such as contentment, and from your tongue only the taste of amrit shines forth, meaning you give teaching that is amrit.
8K0D: Milat = on meeting (Guru Amardas ji). Sant = coolness. Durat = sin. Doorantar = from afar. Nasai = is destroyed.
On having the vision (of Guru Ramdas ji), coolness arises (in the heart), and sin is destroyed from afar (on seeing him).
Meeting with You, a tranquil peace wells up, and sins run far away.
Meeting with you, tranquility wells up and sin flees away from the mortal's mind.
By meeting you, peace arises in the heart, and the mass of sins (durat) is driven far from within.
VY86: Sukh sagar = the ocean of comforts (union with the Lord). Dint = given, (that which was) bestowed (on Guru Ramdas ji). Har mag = on the path of Hari. Na hutai = does not tire.
(Guru Ramdas ji) has attained the ocean of comforts (union with the Lord) given (by Guru Amardas ji); (that is why Guru Ramdas, walking) on the path of Hari, does not tire.
You have attained the Ocean of peace, and You never grow tired on the Lord's path.
Blessed by Guru Amar Dass, you have attained the Ocean of peace and you grow not weary in your God's way.
You have attained Vahiguru, the ocean of comforts. On the path of teaching given (dint) by the True Guru, the third Patshah ji, you do not grow tired (hutai), meaning you keep walking on it.
AP95: Maphutai = does not split, does not break. Sannah = armour. Seel = sweet nature.
(Guru Ramdas ji's) armour of self-restraint, truth, contentment and sweet nature (is such that it) does not break; (that is, he always has these virtues).
The armor of self-restraint, truth, contentment and humility can never be pierced.
The coat-of-mail of your self-restraint, truth, contentment and humility breaks not.

You have put on the armour (sannah) of virtues: self-control (sanjam) of the senses, truth, contentment and a peaceful (seel) nature, which cannot break (maphutai); meaning, you hold the virtues described above.
AFCF: Satgur praman = equal to Guru Amardas ji. Bidhnai = the Ordainer, the Creator. Sirio = has made (Guru Ramdas ji). Jag = the world. Jas toor = the trumpet of glory.
The Creator has made (Guru Ramdas ji) equal to the Guru (Amardas ji); the world has sounded the trumpet of (his) glory.
The Creator Lord certified the True Guru, and now the world blows the trumpet of His Praises.
The Creator-Lord has created the approved True Guru and the world plays the bugle of His praise.
The Timeless Being has created (sirio) you equal (praman) to Satguru Amardas Sahib ji, and has sounded the trumpet (toor) of your glory throughout the whole world.
RX4J: The poet Kalyasahar says: "O Guru Ramdas! You have attained the state of the fearless and imperishable Hari." ||6||
So speaks KALL: O Guru Raam Daas, You have attained the state of fearless immortality. ||6||
Says Kall, you, O Guru Ram Dass, has obtained the eternal and Imperishable status.
Sri 'Kal' utters: Sri Guru Ramdas Sahib ji, you have attained the state of liberation, which is free of fear. ||6||
2BV8: Jitau = has conquered. Satgur praman = like the Guru (Amardas ji).
(Guru Ramdas ji) has conquered the world like the Guru (Amardas ji), and has remembered the One (Timeless Being) in (his) mind.
O certified True Guru, You have conquered the world; You meditate single-mindedly on the One Lord.
O approved True Guru, you have conquered the world and you contemplate the One Lord in your mind.
Like (praman) Sri Guru Amardas Sahib ji, you have conquered the world, and meditated in your mind on the one Vahiguru alone.
6H1J: Blessed is the True Guru Amardas, who firmly implanted the Name (in Guru Ramdas ji).
Blessed, blessed is Guru Amar Daas, the True Guru, who implanted the Naam, the Name of the Lord, deep within.
Blest, blest is Amar Dass, the True Guru, who has enshrined the Name within him.
Blessed is Sri Guru Amardas Sahib ji, who is worthy of being called blessed, who implanted the teaching of the Name in you.
YAGM: Nav nidh = the nine treasures. Nidhan = treasure. Ta kee = of the Guru (Ramdas ji).
(Guru Ramdas ji) has found the treasure of the Name; (as if) the nine treasures have been gained. All the miraculous powers are his handmaids.
The Naam is the wealth of the nine treasures; prosperity and supernatural spiritual powers are His slaves.
The Lord's Name is the treasure of nine sorts of riches, Prosperity and miraculous powers are his hand-maidens.

The treasure (nidhan) of the Name, which gives the nine treasures. All the riddhis and siddhis are handmaids of that Name; meaning, by receiving that Name, riddhis, siddhis and treasures are all your handmaids.
EFHQ: Sahaj sarovar = the ocean of the state of poise, the ocean of peace, the Timeless Being. Purakh = the all-pervading Lord.
(Guru Ramdas ji) has met Hari, the pool of peace; he has met the imperishable, all-pervading Lord.
He is blessed with the ocean of intuitive wisdom; He has met with the Imperishable Lord God.
He is blessed with the ocean of Divine knowledge and has met with the Imperishable Lord.
The True Guru, a pool of the water of wisdom (sahaj), has met you; so the imperishable Being, Vahiguru, has met you, that is, been attained by you.
YYAM: Ad le = from the beginning. Jit lag = attached to which (Name). So = that (Name). Gur = the Guru (Amardas ji).
The Name, attached to which devotees have been crossing over from the very beginning, that Name the Guru (Amardas ji) firmly implanted (in Guru Ramdas ji).
The Guru has implanted the Naam deep within; attached to the Naam, the devotees have been carried across since ancient times.
The Guru has implanted in him the name, attached to which the saints have been ever ferried across since primeval times.
The Name, by taking whose support devotees of old, such as Kabir ji, crossed the ocean of the world: Sri Guru, the third Patshah ji, has implanted that Name in you.
HMSN: The poet Kalyasahar says: 'O Guru Ramdas ji! You have attained the (supreme) treasure of the Timeless Being's love.' ||7||
So speaks KALL: O Guru Raam Daas, You have obtained the wealth of the Lord's Love. ||7||
O Guru Ram Dass, you have attained the wealth of the Lord's love; says Kall, the poet.
Sri 'Kal' ji says: O Sri Guru Ramdas Sahib ji, you have attained the treasure of Hari's love. ||7||
R2DV: Prem bhagat = loving devotion. Parvah = streams, springs. Pubalee = from past births. Hutai = runs out, ends.
Springs of loving devotion to the Timeless Being flow (in Guru Ramdas ji's heart). (The) love from past births (that Guru Ramdas ji has for the Timeless Being) does not run out;
The flow of loving devotion and primal love does not stop.
The low of loving-adoration and the prenatal affection ceases not.
At your door the streams of loving devotion are flowing, because your love for Vahiguru from past births does not tire (na hutai), meaning it does not lessen.
TEKQ: Athah = deep. Amia dhara ras = the taste of the streams of the amrit of the Name. Gutai = drinks in great gulps.
(Through the) fathomless Word of the Guru (Amardas ji), (Guru Ramdas) drinks in the taste of the streams of the amrit of the Name in great gulps.
The True Guru drinks in the stream of nectar, the sublime essence of the Shabad, the Infinite Word of God.
The True Guru in-drinks the Nectar of the immortalising stream of the Infinite Lord.
O True Guru ji! You are gulping down (gutai) the taste of the stream of amrit that is the fathomless bliss of Brahm, meaning you are drinking it.
DSZL: Sar sahaj = in the pool of poise, in the pool of spiritual steadiness. Samayau = is absorbed.

(Lofty) understanding is (Guru Ramdas ji's) mother and contentment (his) father (that is, he was born and raised in these virtues; he has lofty understanding and is completely contented). (Guru Ramdas) is always immersed in the pool of peace.
Wisdom is His mother, and contentment is His father; He is absorbed in the ocean of intuitive peace and poise.
Wisdom is his mother, contentment his father and he is merged in the ocean of equipoise.

Excellent understanding is your mother and contentment your father; the meaning is that it is as if your form was born from these virtues; or, by holding these virtues, your form becomes manifest in the heart. And your mind is absorbed in the pool (sar) of peace (sahaj).
BEXD: Ajonee = free of births. Sambhaviau = self-illumined. Gur bachan = through the True Guru's word.
(Guru Ramdas) is the form of Hari, who is free of births and self-illumined. (He) has carried the world across through the True Guru's word.
The Guru is the Embodiment of the Unborn, Self-illumined Lord; by the Word of His Teachings, the Guru carries the world across.
The Guru is the embodiment of the unborn and self-illumined Lord and by his word ferries the world across.

Vahiguru, who is free of births: in that form you have fully come into being (sambhaviau), meaning you have become that very form. So, O True Guru ji, through your words you have carried the beings of the world across.
A9U3: Abigat = unmanifest, unseen. Agochar = beyond the reach of the senses. Apar = beyond the beyond, infinite.
(Guru Ramdas) is the form of the unseen, imperceptible and infinite Hari. (He has) enshrined the True Guru's Word in (his) mind.
Within His mind, the Guru has enshrined the Shabad, the Word of the Unseen, Unfathomable, Infinite Lord.
Within his mind, the Guru has enshrined the Name of the Unseen and Unapprehensible Transcendent Lord.
Vahiguru, who is not an object (abigat) of mind and speech, beyond the reach of the eyes and other senses, and beyond (apar) all worlds: you have enshrined him in your heart through the Guru's Word.
PFHY: Jagat udharan = the Timeless Being who carries the world across. ||8||
The poet Kalyasahar says, 'O Guru Ramdas! You have found the Timeless Being who carries the world across.' ||8||
So speaks KALL: O Guru Raam Daas, You have attained the Lord, the Saving Grace of the world. ||8||
Says Kall, O Guru Ram Dass, you have attained to God, the Saviour of the world.
Sri 'Kal' ji says: O Sri Guru Ramdas Sahib ji! You have attained Sri Akal Purakh ji, who delivers the world. ||8||
WJ6Z: Nav nidhan = the treasure of the nine (treasures). Bhagatah = for the devotees. Bhav = the world-ocean. Taran = able to carry across.
Able to carry devotees across the world-ocean, a storehouse of the treasures, able to carry the world across,
The Saving Grace of the world, the nine treasures, carries the devotees across the world-ocean.
God's Name is the Deliverer of the universe, the Giver of nine treasures and ferries the saints across the world ocean.
Vahiguru's Name, which delivers the world, is the home of the nine treasures, and carries devotees across the world-ocean.
LJ4G: Har nam = Hari's Name. Bis = the whole world (vishva). Bikhai = poison. Nivaran = able to remove.
(With True Guru Ramdas ji) Hari's Name is (as it were) a drop of amrit, which can remove the poison of the whole world.
The Drop of Ambrosial Nectar, the Lord's Name, is the antidote to the poison of sin.
The ambrosial drop of the Lord's Name is an antidote to the poison of sins.
Hari's Name is like a drop of amrit, which removes the poison of desire of the whole world.
QANM: Guru Ramdas is a fine tree of spiritual poise that has borne fruit; (this tree) bears fruits of amrit that give wisdom.
The tree of intuitive peace and poise blossoms and bears the ambrosial fruit of spiritual wisdom.
The tree of equipoise blossoms and bears the ambrosial fruit of Divine knowledge.
Through that Name, the tree of peace (sahaj) has borne fruit, and on it hang fruits of amrit, which are virtues such as wisdom.
22VF: Paeeahi = are obtained. Dhann = fortunate. Te jan = those people.
(These fruits) are obtained by the Guru's grace, and those people are blessed and very fortunate (who have obtained them).
Blessed are those fortunate people who receive it, by Guru's Grace.
Blessed and very fortunate are those persons, who receive it by the Guru's grace.
O True Guru ji! That Name described above is obtained by your grace, and those who have obtained it are very fortunate, blessed people.
SGZE: Te mukte = those people have crossed over. Sabad = by the blessing of the Word. Man = in the mind. Gur parcha = love for the Guru.
Those people have been liberated by the blessing of the True Guru's Word, who have found love for the Guru (Ramdas ji) in their minds.
They are liberated through the Shabad, the Word of the True Guru; their minds are filled with the Guru's Wisdom.
They are emancipated through the word of the True Guru and their mind receives wisdom from the Guru's.
O True Guru ji! Those people who have found their minds absorbed in your Word have been liberated from the world.
3JDV: Sabad neesan = the drum of the Word. ||9||
The poet Kalyasahar says, 'O Guru Ramdas! You have beaten the drum of the Word.' ||9||
So speaks KALL: O Guru Raam Daas, You beat the drum of the Shabad. ||9||
Says Kall, O Guru Ram Dass, you have struck the drum of the Lord's Name.
Sri 'Kal' ji says: O Sri Guru Ramdas Sahib ji! To carry beings across, you have beaten the drum (neesan) of teaching (sabad). ||9||

CNXS: Sadha = faith, trust. Sahaj = peace, steadiness, spiritual poise. Chhavan = canopy. Saraichau = screen wall of a tent. Sada seel = always staying sweet-natured. Sannah = armour. Sohai = looks beautiful, adorns.
(Guru Ramdas ji has) made faith a bed (for the Lord); the steadiness of (his) heart is the canopy, contentment is the tent wall, and constant sweetness of nature is the armour.
On the bed of faith, with the blankets of intuitive peace and poise and the canopy of contentment, You are embellished forever with the armor of humility.
You, O Guru, have the couch of faith, the bedding of equipoise and the canopy of contentment and the armour of humility ever embellishes you.

O True Guru ji! Your bed of faith (sadha) is spread out, the canopy of wisdom (sahaj) is stretched over you, the tent wall (saraichau) of contentment is set up, and the armour (sannah) of a peaceful (seel) nature, worn on your body, adorns you.
25FJ: Gur sabad = through the Guru's Word. Samacharo = has practised. Tek = support (of the True Guru). Sangad = companions and others. Bohai = makes fragrant.
By the blessing of the Guru's (Amardas ji's) Word, (he) has practised (it); (the Guru's) support makes (his) companions and others fragrant.
Through the Word of the Guru's Shabad, you practice the Naam; You lean on its Support, and give Your Fragrance to Your companions.
Through the Guru's word, you practise the Name and leaning on it alone, you perfume yours comrades.

Such a hero you are, Maharaj! You have well (sam) gathered (acharo) the treasure of teaching of the True Guru, the third Patshah ji; and taking the Name alone as your support (tek), like a pillow, you have made fragrant (bohai) with your glory those people who have been your companions from the start (ad), meaning who became Sikhs.
MNWY: Ajoneeu = free of births. Bhalyu = good. Amal = (a-mal) without stain, pure.
Guru Ramdas is free of birth (and death), good, and pure of soul.
You abide with the Unborn Lord, the Good and Pure True Guru.
You abide with Amar Dass, the birth-free, and sublime True Guru, free from any blemish.
O True Guru! By living with the third Patshah and doing good deeds (amal), you have become free of births.
D6C9: Tua = your. Bas = dwelling. Sahaj sarovar = in the pool of spiritual poise. ||10||
The poet Kalyasahar says, 'O Guru Ramdas! Your dwelling is in the pool of spiritual poise.' ||10||
So speaks KALL: O Guru Raam Daas, You abide in the sacred pool of intuitive peace and poise. ||10||
Says Kall, the bard, you, O Guru Ram Dass, abide in the ocean of Divine knowledge.
Sri Kal ji says: Sri Guru Ramdas Sahib ji, you dwell always in the pool of wisdom. ||10||
19DZ: Jinh kau = on which people. Ridai = in (their) hearts. Nivasai = makes dwell.
The people on whom the True Guru is pleased, (in their) hearts he makes the Name of the Timeless Being dwell.
The Lord's Name abides in the hearts of those who are pleasing to the Guru.
They, on whom is the pleasure of the Guru; the Lord's Name abides in their mind.
Those with whom the Guru is well pleased have Hari's Name dwelling in their hearts.
ZE4M: The people on whom the Guru is pleased, sin flees (from them) from afar (on seeing them).
Sins run far away from those who are pleasing to the Guru.
The sins run away from them, with whom the Guru is mightily pleased.
Those with whom the True Guru is well pleased, their sins (durat) flee far from within the heart (doorantar).
QDPD: The people with whom the True Guru is pleased, he removes their ego.
Those who are pleasing to the Guru eradicate pride and egotism from within.
They, on whom is the pleasure of the Guru, they do away with self-pride and self-conceit.
Those with whom the True Guru is well pleased, he removes vices such as pride and arrogance from their hearts.
JK8Z: Sabad lag = joining to the Word. Bhavjal = the world-ocean. Tarai = carries across.
The people on whom the Guru shows grace, he joins to the Word and carries across this world-ocean.
Those who are pleasing to the Guru are attached to the Shadad, the Word of God; they are carried across the terrifying world-ocean.
They, with whom the Guru is greatly pleased, attached to the Name, they are ferried across the world ocean.
The people with whom the True Guru is pleased, he attaches to his teaching and carries across the world-ocean.
6VGZ: Parchau = teaching. Praman = authentic, accepted. Gur = of the Guru. Tin janam = their birth. Sakaythau = fruitful. Jag = in the world.
The people who have received the True Guru's authentic teaching, their birth in the world has become fruitful.
Those who are blessed with the wisdom of the certified Guru - blessed and fruitful is their birth into the world.
Whosoever is blessed with the gnosis of the approved Guru, fruitful is his advent in this world.
O Sri Guru Ramdas Sahib ji! Those who have found absorption in your true (praman) Word, their birth in the world has become fruitful (sakaythau).
S5AT: Bhaj = fall (at). Kaly kab = O poet Kalyasahar! Bhugat = worldly goods. Guru lag = by falling at the Guru's refuge. ||11||
O poet Kalyasahar! Fall at the True Guru's refuge; only by falling at the Guru's refuge (can) liberation and all goods (be had). ||11||
KALL the poet runs to the Sanctuary of the Great Guru; attached to the Guru, they are blessed with worldly enjoyments, liberation and everything. ||11||
Poet Kall hastens to the protection of the sire Guru. Attached to the Guru one is all blessed with the worldly prosperity, spiritual emancipation and every-thing.

Sri 'Kal' the poet says: O mind! Or, O brother! Hurry (bhaj) to the refuge of such a True Guru, that is, reach it, because all things, enjoyment and liberation and the rest, are gained by meeting the True Guru. ||11||
USYV: Satgur = the Guru (Ramdas ji). Khema = canopy. Jug jooth = the multitude of ages, all the ages. Samane = have come under (that is, under the canopy).

The True Guru (Ramdas ji) has stretched a canopy (of the Timeless Being's praise); all the ages (that is, the beings of all the ages) have come to rest under it (that is, all beings have begun to sing Hari's praise).
The Guru has pitched the tent; under it, all the ages are gathered.
The True Guru has pitched the tent underneath which, heave gathered all the men.
O True Guru ji! You have stretched over the world the canopy (khema) of Vahiguru's glory, under which the beings of this Kaliyug have gathered in crowd after crowd (jooth).
Z54N: Anbhau = wisdom (anubhav, direct experience). Jit = through which. Aghane = are satisfied.
Wisdom is the lance (in his hand), the Name of the Timeless Being is (his) support, by whose blessing all are satisfied.
He carries the spear of intuition, and takes the Support of Naam, the Name of the Lord, through which the devotees are fulfilled.
Recondite intuition is his banner and the Lord's Name his support, with which the saints are satiated.
The direct realisation of the Form of experience is the lance (neja) in your hand, and the support of the Name is your pillow; through that Name the devotees are fulfilled (aghane).
4SLA: Har sang = in the Timeless Being. Samane = have merged.
(By the blessing of the support of Hari's Name) Guru Nanak Dev ji, Guru Angad Sahib, Guru Amardas ji and other devotees have merged in the Timeless Being.
Guru Nanak, Guru Angad and Guru Amar Daas, through devotional worship, have merged into the Lord.
Through loving-adoration, Guru Nanak, Angad and Amar Dass, have been blended with the Lord.
Through devotion to Sri Guru Nanak Dev ji, Sri Guru Angad Sahib ji, and through devotion to Sri Guru Angad Sahib ji, Sri Guru Amardas Sahib ji, merged with Hari, that is, became one with him.
AXCS: Gur Ramdas = O Guru Ramdas! Tumh hoo = you too. Raj jog ras = the taste of raj jog. Jane = have known. ||12||
O Guru Ramdas ji! You too have recognised this taste of raj jog. ||12||
O Guru Raam Daas, You alone know the taste of this Raja Yoga. ||12||
You alone, O Guru Ram Dass, know the relish of this union with God, the King.
Through devotion to that Sri Guru Amardas Sahib ji, O Sri Guru Ramdas Sahib! You alone know (jane) the joyful taste of this raj jog, the yoga of wisdom. ||12||
AV1E: Soi = is that one. Jin = who. Jania = has recognised (the Timeless Being). Unman = in the state of complete bloom. Rath = the flow of the mind. Dharia = has placed, has steadied.
Janak is the one who has come to know (the Timeless Being), who has steadied the flow of his mind in complete bloom,
He alone is enlightened like Janaka, who links the chariot of his mind to the state of ecstatic realization.
He alone is the divine, who hitches his mind chariot to the most sublime state and realises his Lord.

You are that Janak, the father of the world in the form of Vishnu, who have known your own true form. As it is said: "Whoever knows him becomes like him." ☬ And you have stopped the chariot of your mind's flowing attention in the fourth state (unman).
Z2M0: Samachare = has gathered, has practised. Abhara = not filled. Sar = pool. Abhara sar = the pool that can never be filled, the mind that is never satisfied. Bharia = filled, satisfied.
Who has gathered truth and contentment (within), and who has satisfied this mind that is never satisfied.
He gathers in truth and contentment, and fills up the empty pool within.
He gathers truth and contentment and fills the empty tank of his mind.
You have well (sam) taken up (achare) virtues such as truth and contentment, and you have filled with the water of love the heart-pool of the Sikhs, which was empty (abhara).
BPKY: Akath = that which cannot be described. Amra puri = the city that lasts forever, the eternal abode, the steady spiritual state. Akath katha amra puri = this deep matter of the state of poise. Jis = the person to whom. Dei = (the Timeless Being) gives.

This (above-mentioned) deep matter of the steady spiritual state (that is, Janak's state) is attained only by the person to whom the Timeless Being gives it (that is, such a Janak-state is not given to everyone).
He speaks the Unspoken Speech of the eternal city. He alone obtains it, to whom God gives it.
Ineffable is the discourse of the immortal city that is attained by those who are blessed by the Lord.
The discourse on the indescribable (akath) Vahiguru, which gives the immortal city, is going on in your court; whoever you give it to receives it.
KJE2: O Guru Ramdas! This rule of Janak suits only you (that is, only you are worthy of this spiritual poise). ||13||
O Guru Raam Daas, Your sovereign rule, like that of Janak, is Yours alone. ||13||
O Guru Ram Dass, the kingship like that of Janak, becomes you alone.
So this (rule of Janak) is the light of wisdom; Sri Guru Ramdas Sahib ji, it suits only you, meaning it adorns you. ||13||
A6PZ: Japai = (each person who) chants. Drirh = with faith, firmly. Man = in the mind. Ek liv = with a one-pointed mind, with attention joined. Tinh jan = to those people. Kahu = say. Kat = when?
Each person who chants the True Guru's Name in the mind with faith and attention joined: tell me, sir, when can pain and sin touch them?
Tell me, how can sin and suffering cling to that humble being who chants the Naam, given by the Guru, with single-minded love and firm faith?
Whosoever steadfastly recites the True Guru-given Name with single mindedness and love, say, how can suffering and sin cling to that man?

O brother! Whoever chants the Name through such a True Guru, making the mind's attention one-pointed (ek liv) and with firmness, that is, with certainty, tell me, where are pain and sin for those people? That is, there are none.
GPLV: Drist dharai = looks with a gracious glance. Rid = in the heart. Khovai = destroys. Taran taran = a ship to carry the world across. Taran = ship.

(The True Guru, who) is (as it were) a ship to carry the world across: the person on whom he casts a glance of grace even for an instant reflects on (the Guru's) Word in the heart and loses lust and anger (from within).

When the Lord, the Boat to carry us across, bestows His Glance of Grace, even for an instant, the mortal contemplates the Shabad within his heart; unfulfilled sexual desire and unresolved anger are eradicated.
On whomsoever God, the ship to ferry across, casts His merciful glance even for a trice, He contemplates the Name in his mind and is rid of lust and wrath.

O brother! The True Guru is like a ship (taran) to carry one across the world; on whomever he casts a glance of grace even for an instant, that person reflects on the Word in the heart, (and so) loses vices such as lust and anger.
X88C: Jeean sabhan = of all beings. Agam = unreachable. Bikhyata = one who reveals. Ahinis = day and night, at all times. Ahi = day. Nis = night. Dhavai = holds. Na sovai = is not negligent.
(True Guru Ramdas) is the giver of all beings and reveals the wisdom of the unreachable Hari; day and night he holds Hari in meditation and is not negligent even for an instant.
The Guru is the Giver to all beings; He speaks the spiritual wisdom of the Unfathomable Lord, and meditates on Him day and night. He never sleeps, even for an instant.
The Guru is the blesser of all the beings, recites the gnosis of the Unfathomable Lord, e ver contemplates Him and sleeps not even for a while.

The wisdom of Vahiguru, the giver of all beings, unreachable by mind and speech, becomes manifest (bikhata) in that person's heart. So that person's attention runs continuously (ahinis) to meditation on that form, because they do not sleep even for an instant.
ZJSC: Ja kau = the person whose. Dekhat = on seeing (the Guru). Gyan = through (the Guru's) wisdom.
The Gurmukh who washes away the filth of their evil understanding through the wisdom (given by Guru Ramdas) gains the treasure of the Name, and their poverty is removed by having his vision.
Seeing Him, poverty vanishes, and one is blessed with the treasure of the Naam, the Name of the Lord. The spiritual wisdom of the Guru's Word washes away the filth of evil-mindedness.
Such is the Guru, seeing whom poverty vanishes and one is blessed with the Name-like treasure. The Divine knowledge imparted by the supreme Guru washed off the filth of the evil-intellect.

On seeing Sri Guru Ramdas Sahib ji, poverty goes away, and the being gains the Name, the home of the treasures; so, gaining wisdom through such a True Guru, the being washes away the filth of a false understanding.
F6SS: Each person who chants the True Guru's (Ramdas's) Name in the mind with faith and attention joined: tell me, sir, can sin and pain touch them? ||1||
Tell me, how can sin and suffering cling to that humble being who chants the Naam, given by the Guru, with single-minded love and firm faith? ||1||
How can suffering and sin cling to that person who steadfastly recites the Name with love and focused mint that is given by the True Guru?

O brother! Whoever chants the Name through such a True Guru, making the mind's attention one-pointed (ek liv) and with firmness, that is, with certainty, tell me, where are pain and sin for those people? That is, there are none. ||1||
9MX0: Paee hai = on obtaining, on meeting.
On meeting the perfect Guru (Ramdas ji), all dharam and karam (are gained);
Dharmic faith and the karma of good deeds are obtained from the Perfect True Guru.
Faith and good deeds are obtained from the perfect True Guru.

Only through the perfect True Guru is dharam and karam gained. The meaning is that the fruit of karam and dharam, true knowledge of the self, is gained through True Gurus who are learned in scripture and established in Brahm.
3R3H: Ja kee = whose, Guru Ramdas ji's. Jachahi = beg for. Sur = gods. Sar = excellent.
Siddhas, holy men, silent sages, gods and humans beg for the service of this (Guru Ramdas); (his) Word is excellent, and (he has) joined his attention to the One (Timeless Being).
The Siddhas and Holy Saadhus, the silent sages and angelic beings, yearn to serve Him; through the most excellent Word of the Shabad, they are lovingly attuned to the One Lord.
Such is the Lord, for whose service crave the adepts, saints, silent sages and the angelic persons and through whose sublime Name, man is attuned to the One God.

The True Guru whose service gods (sur), humans, siddhas and silent sages all beg of the Supreme Lord, and through whose excellent (sar) teaching all of them have fixed their attention on the one Vahiguru.
684W: Ko = who? Tera = your (limit). Kathanhar = fit to be told. Tujhahi = you alone. Bujhaee hai = has understood, has gained wisdom.
(O Guru Ramdas!) Who can find your (limit)? You are (the form of) the infinite, fearless, Formless One. You alone have received the wisdom of the indescribable Hari, who is worth telling of.
Who can know Your limits? You are the Embodiment of the Fearless, Formless Lord. You are the Speaker of the Unspoken Speech; You alone understand this.
Again, who can know your limit, O Guru? You are the embodiment of the Fear-free and Formless Lord. You alone describe the Ineffable God and you alone are blessed with His comprehension.

O True Guru ji! Who can know the near and far shore of your infinity (apar)? That is, no one can know it. So, O fearless, Formless One! Teller of the indescribable Vahiguru! Only you have come to understand that Timeless Being.
20EX: Sansar = O world. O worldly being! Sanghar = death. Chhutahu = be saved. Dand kal = punishment, rebuke. Dhyaee hai = should meditate, should remember.
O worldly being, lost in doubts! Taking the Guru's (Ramdas ji's) teaching, remember (the Lord's Name); you will be saved from birth and death, and there will be no rebuke from Yama either.
O foolish worldly mortal, you are deluded by doubt; give up birth and death, and you shall not be punished by the Messenger of Death. Meditate on the Guru's Teachings.
O worldly doubt-strayed man lost in doubt, reflect you on your Lord by the Guru's instruction. Thiswise you shall be delivered of birth and death and the death's courier shall punish you not.

So we teach thus: O beings of the world, lost in doubt! Make such an effort that you are freed from the round (sanghar) of births. ☬ Question: What is that effort? ☬ Answer: When you take the Guru's teaching and meditate (dhyaee hai) on that Vahiguru, then Yama's rod of death will not be over you; meaning, you will be free of birth and death.
LHHR: Mugadh = foolish. Beechar = reflect. Ahinis = day and night, at all times. Jap = remember. ||2||
O foolish mind! O foolish being! Reflect, and remember (the Name) day and night. On meeting the perfect True Guru (Ramdas ji), (all) dharam and karam (are gained). ||2||
You foolish mortal being, reflect on this in your mind; chant and meditate day and night. Dharmic faith and the karma of good deeds are obtained from the Perfect True Guru. ||2||
O silly mortal, reflect, reflect you in your mind and, day and night, recite you, your Lord's Name. Faith and good deed are obtained from the perfect True Guru.

So, O foolish being! Reflect in your mind, see the world as false, and chant Vahiguru's Name day and night through the True Guru, because only from that perfect True Guru is wisdom, the fruit of dharam and karam, gained. ||2||
7ZWU: Hau = I. Bal bal jau = may I be a sacrifice, may I be devoted.
I am a sacrifice to the Name of the true True Guru (Ramdas ji).
I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to the True Name, O my True Guru.
O my True Guru, I am a sacrifice, yea, O sacrifice to True Name.
O True Guru ji! With mind and speech I am a sacrifice to your true Name.
6WXR: Deu = (that) I may give. Sareu = (that) I may do. Rasna = with the tongue. Rasahu = chant. Jug kar = both hands. Jor = joining. Ek mukh = facing (him).

What comparison can I give (that is, how can I say what he is like), what service can I do? (O my mind!) With both hands joined, facing (him), remember (him) with the tongue (that alone is the comparison and that alone is the service).
What Praises can I offer to You? What service can I do for You? I have only one mouth and tongue; with my palms pressed together, I chant to You with joy and delight.
What praise can I attribute to you and what service of yours can I perform with the one tongue of my mouth, I joyful recite your Name clasping both of my hands.

What comparison can I give you, and what service can I do (sareu)? The meaning is that your comparison cannot be told, and no service is seen by which I could please you. So with the one tongue of my mouth and both hands joined, may I become absorbed (rasahu) in chanting your Name alone.
NRQZ: Phun = and further. Jan = recognise. Anat = any other. Man = believe in, worship, chant. Sar = excellent. Gur = the Guru (Ramdas ji). Rid = of the heart. Dhar = support.

O poet Nalya! And further (do this): through your mind, words and deeds make (that Name) firm, and do not chant any other; that Guru (Ramdas ji) has made that infinite and excellent Name the support of your heart,
In thought, word and deed, I know the Lord; I do not worship any other. The Guru has enshrined the most excellent Name of the Infinite Lord within my heart.
Again, in your thought, word and deed, you realise the True Name and adore not any other. O Guru, you have enshrined within my mind the sublime Name of the Infinite Lord.

In mind and speech I know you to be the form of the Supreme Lord and believe in no other (anat). Because the excellent (sach [sic: the line reads 'sar']) Name of the infinite Vahiguru, given by you, I have held in my heart.

TQNB: Paras = touch. Kanchana = gold. Hui = becomes. Chandana subas = the fragrance of sandalwood. An tar = in other trees. Jas = whose (Name).
By remembering him (one becomes as) glass becomes gold at the touch of the philosopher's stone, and (at the touch of sandalwood) other trees take on the fragrance of sandalwood.

So speaks NALL the poet: touching the Philosopher's Stone, glass is transformed into gold, and the sandalwood tree imparts its fragrance to other trees; meditating in remembrance on the Lord, I am transformed.
Says Nall, the poet, just as by touching philosopher's stone, glass becomes gold and just as sandal imparts fragrance to other trees, similar is the Guru, whose contemplation transmutes the mortal.

Sri 'Nal' the poet says: O Sri Guru Amardas Sahib ji! We beings, worthless as glass, by touching you, the philosopher's stone, become priceless like gold (kanchana). And by the fragrance of the sandalwood of remembering you, other beings, like ordinary trees, become sandalwood of the finest fragrance; the meaning is that those people become saints.
KXCL: Duare = door, gateway. Nivare = are removed. ||3||
On seeing the door of that Guru (Ramdas ji), lust, anger (and all the rest) are removed; I am a sacrifice to the Name of that true Guru. ||3||
Seeing His Door, I am rid of sexual desire and anger. I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to the True Name, O my True Guru. ||3||
I am a sacrifice yea, a sacrifice to the True Name of the True Guru, seeing whose door, one is rid of lust and wrath.
O Sri Guru Ramdas Sahib ji! Through your vision we have removed all the vices such as lust and anger. O True Guru ji! With mind and speech I am a sacrifice to your true Name. ||3||
XMUU: Deean = dia un, he (Hari) gave. Gur Ramdas = to Guru Ramdas ji.
That (Timeless Being) has given Guru Ramdas (ji) the throne of raj and jog.
Guru Raam Daas was blessed with the Throne of Raja Yoga.
Guru Amar Dass has blessed Guru Ram Dass with the temporal and spiritual throne.
O Sri Guru Ramdas Sahib ji! This throne of raj jog that the True Gurus have given you:
NFJV: Prathme = first. Chand = moon. Anand = joy. Taran = to carry across. Pragas = light.
First Guru Nanak Dev ji (appeared) as the moon; (he) gave light to carry people across, and (the whole) world was filled with joy.
First, Guru Nanak illuminated the world, like the full moon, and filled it with bliss. To carry humanity across, He bestowed His Radiance.
As first Nanak Dev became manifest like the moon. To emancipate the human beings, he illumined the world, which was then filled with bliss.

First Sri Guru Nanak Dev ji rose like the moon, and by his taking birth there was bliss in the whole world. Seated on this throne of Guruship, he spread the light of wisdom to carry his servants across the world-ocean.
UZA8: Deeau = gave. Nidhan = treasure. Akath = indescribable. Panch bhoot = the five enemies (such as lust). Jamat na = does not arise. Tras = fear. Keene = made.

(Then Guru Nanak Dev) blessed Guru Angad Dev ji with the treasure of wisdom of Hari's indescribable story, (so that Guru Angad Dev) brought the five enemies such as lust under control, and (he) had no fear (of them).
He blessed Guru Angad with the treasure of spiritual wisdom, and the Unspoken Speech; He overcame the five demons and the fear of the Messenger of Death.
With the treasure of the Divine discourse and gnosis of the Ineffable Lord, Nanak blessed Guru Angad, who overcame his five demos and was rid of the fear of the Death's courier.

That Maharaj, the first Patshahi ji, gave Sri Guru Angad Sahib ji the Name, the home of the treasures, or the throne of Guruship, and gave him the wisdom of the story of the indescribable (akath) Vahiguru. So, seated on this throne, Sri Guru Angad Sahib ji brought the five demons, lust, anger and the rest, under control, so that no fear ever arises (jamat na) again.
9H2A: Pat = honour. Aghan = sins. Gat = went away. Jas = whose (Guru Amardas ji's).
(Then, by Guru Angad Dev's touch) Sri Satguru Guru Amardas (appeared); (he) kept the honour of the Kaliyug; on seeing his lotus feet, (the Kaliyug's) sins fled.
The Great and True Guru, Guru Amar Daas, has preserved honor in this Dark Age of Kali Yuga. Seeing His Lotus Feet, sin and evil are destroyed.
The great and venerable True Guru, Amar Dass saved the honour of the Darkage and such is he, seeing whose lotus feet, men's sins are destroyed.

Then Sri Guru Angad Sahib ji kept the honour of Sri Satgur Amardas Sahib ji in the Kaliyug, meaning he made his service fruitful, that is, he was seated on this throne. What is that Maharaj like? By seeing the lotus feet of Sri Amardas ji, all the multitudes of sins (aghan) are destroyed (gat).
4SRC: Sabh bidh = in every way, completely. Manyio = was convinced. ||4||
(When Guru Amardas ji's) mind was completely convinced, then (he) was pleased (with Guru Ramdas ji), and (he) blessed Guru Ramdas with the throne of raj and jog. ||4||
When His mind was totally satisfied in every way, when He was totally pleased, He bestowed upon Guru Raam Daas the Throne of Raja Yoga. ||4||
When his mind was satisfied in every way, then was he pleased and he bestowed on Guru Ram Dass, the secular and spiritual throne.
When the mind of that Sri Guru Amardas Sahib ji was satisfied with you in every way, then, O Sri Guru Ramdas Sahib ji, he gave you this throne of raj jog. ||4|| ☬ He utters the rad and other metres:
5DYP: it is the Name of measure.
BD6A: Jisahi = the Hari-Name which. Dharyau = has kept steady. Viom = sky. Te = those (plural). Neer sar = the water of the pools. Avar = and. Anal = fire. Anad = food and the rest. Keeau = has created.
The Hari-Name that has held the earth and sky steady, and that has created air, those waters of the pools, fire, food and the rest,
He established the earth, the sky and the air, the water of the oceans, fire and food.
He who has installed the earth and the sky and air and the water of the oceans and has make the fire and corn etc.

Vahiguru, who has held up the earth, the sky (viom) and the air, meaning established them in his order, and made fire (anal) and the ocean (sar) of water, or pools, and also the whole range of things such as food (anad).
VLCL: Taroo = trees. Sail = mountains. Sas = the moon. Rikh = the stars. Nis = at night. Soor = the sun. Din = by day.
(By whose blessing) the moon and stars (rise) at night and the sun by day; who has made the mountains and given fruit and flowers to the trees.
He created the moon, the starts and the sun, night and day and mountains; he blessed the trees with flowers and fruits.
Who has created the moon, the stars the sun, night, the day and the mountains and who has blessed the trees with flowers and fruits.
Creating the moon (sas), the stars (rikh), the night (nis), the sun (soor), the day, the mountains (sail) and the rest, he has given fruit and flowers to the trees (taroo).
8Y2P: Sur = gods. Nar = humans. Sapat = seven. Kia = made. Dhario = has held up. Jas = who.
Who has created gods, humans and the seven seas, and has held up the three worlds,
He created the gods, human beings and the seven seas; He established the three worlds.
Who has created the gods, men and the seven oceans and who has established the three worlds.
Vahiguru, who made the gods, humans, the seven seas and the rest, and whose Name has held up these three worlds; meaning, the Name that is the support of these three worlds.
EMKB: That one Hari-Name alone is eternal; (Guru Ramdas ji found that very) light (of the Name) from Guru Amardas ji. ||1||5||
Guru Amar Daas was blessed with the Light of the One Name, the True Name of the Lord. ||1||5||
Guru Amar Dass is blessed with the light of that unique Name, the Lord's True Name.
The one Name of Hari is well known; that light of the Name you have surely (sat) received from Sri Guru Amardas Sahib ji. ||1||5||
J3MH: Kachahu = from glass. Sabad gur = the Guru's Word. Sravanahi = with the ears.
(The person who) has heard the Guru's Word with their ears has (as it were) turned from glass into gold.
Glass is transformed into gold, listening to the Word of the Guru's Shabad.
Hearing the Guru's word with the ears, glass is transformed into gold.

O True Guru ji! The person who has heard your teaching (sabad) through the ears has become like gold (kanchan) from glass; meaning, one who was devoid of good virtues has become the pure form of Brahm.
8MF8: Bikh = poison. Mukh = with the mouth. Bhaniau = uttered.
Whoever has uttered the True Guru's Name with their mouth has turned from poison into amrit.
Poison is transformed into ambrosial nectar, speaking the Name of the True Guru.
Reciting the True Guru's Name with the mouth, poison is transmuted into Nectar.
O True Guru! Whoever, through your teaching, has uttered the Name with their mouth has become amrit from poison.
YCYC: Lohau = from iron. Jad = if. Nadar dharai = looks, casts a glance.
If the True Guru casts (a gracious) glance, (a being) turns from iron into a ruby.
Iron is transformed into jewels, when the True Guru bestows His Glance of Grace.
When the True Guru casts his merciful glance, iron is turned into a jewel.
O True Guru ji! When you cast a glance of grace, then a being that was cheap, or inert, meaning full of desires or heavy with sins, becomes priceless like a ruby.
FZ63: Pahan = stone. Beecharai = reflecting. Manak = pearl.
The people who have reflected on and chanted the wisdom told by the Guru, the Guru (as it were) turns them from stones into gems.
Stones are transformed into emeralds, when the mortal chants and contemplates the spiritual wisdom of the Guru.
When man recites and reflects upon the Guru gnosis, the stone is turned into an emerald.
O True Guru ji! Whoever reflects on the wisdom you have uttered, even if that person was like an ordinary stone, you have made them rare like a gem.
7YZF: Kathahu = from wood. Sreekhand = sandalwood. Satgur = the True Guru. Tin ke = of those people. Gaia = go away.
The pains and poverty of those people have gone away, and the True Guru has (as it were) turned them from wood into sandalwood,
The True Guru transforms ordinary wood into sandalwood, eradicating the pains of poverty.
Eradicates are the pangs and poverty of those, whom the True Guru has make sandal from wood.

O True Guru ji! Those who were like wood, you have made like sandalwood (sreekhand); meaning, those who were without devotion and without glory you have made devoted and glorious. And the whole mass of their pain and poverty has gone away.
HXL1: Jinh = the people who. Se = those people (plural). ||2||6||
Those who have touched the True Guru's feet have turned from animals and ghosts into gods and humans. ||2||6||
Whoever touches the Feet of the True Guru, is transformed from a beast and a ghost into an angelic being. ||2||6||
Whosoever touches the True Guru's feet, becomes an angelic person from beast and ghost.

O True Guru ji! Whoever has touched your lotus feet has become a god (sur) from an animal and a human (nar) from a ghost; or, from animals and ghosts has become the chief (nar), the crown, even among the gods. ||2||6||
A971: Jam = when. Val hoi = takes one's side, helps. Dhanahi = in wealth, because of wealth. Garav = pride. Dijai = gives, does. Kia garav = what pride? (meaning, no pride).
When the True Guru takes (someone's) side, they feel no pride because of wealth.
One who has the Guru on his side - how could he be proud of his wealth?
How can a person be proud of worldly wealth, on whose side is the Guru?
When (jam) the True Guru himself takes someone's side (val), what pride can wealth give them? Meaning, it cannot give any.
LW96: Lakh bahe = hundreds of thousands of arms, hundreds of thousands of armies. Kia kijai = what harm can they do?
When the Guru is on one's side, what harm can hundreds of thousands of armies do?
One who has the Guru on his side - what would hundreds of thousands of supporters do for him?
He, on whose side is the Guru, what harm can lacs of arms do to aim?
For one whose side the Guru ji takes, what can hundreds of thousands of arms and brothers do? That is, they can give no help to that person.
K7D0: Anan par = not toward any other. Anan = not another, no other. Par = toward, devoted to.
When the Guru takes one's side, a person, being given the gift of wisdom and meditation, gives their love to no other (but Hari).
One who has the Guru on his side, does not depend on anyone else for spiritual wisdom and meditation.
He, on whose side is the Guru, for gnosis and spiritual vision, he depends not on my other.
When the True Guru takes one's side, this being stays intent on wisdom and meditation, rare (anan); meaning, becomes watchful.
6F3T: Sakhee = becomes manifest, becomes revealed in the heart. Su = that person. Sachah ghar = in the home of the eternal Lord (comes to rest).
When the Guru helps, the Word becomes manifest in the being's heart, and they (come to rest) in the home of the True Hari.
One who has the Guru on his side contemplates the Shabad and the Teachings, and abides in the Home of Truth.
He, on whose side is the Guru, reflects on the Guru's word and instruction and abides in the True Abode.
When the True Guru takes one's side, it is gained in the home of the being's inner self. That person then recites the Lord's sabads and sakhis in the true home, the congregation of the true.
B5PS: Ahi nis = day and night. Ahi = day. Nis = night. Das bhat = servant (Nalh) the Bhatt.
The servant (Nalya) the Bhatt prays that whoever chants 'Guru, Guru' day and night,
The Lord's humble slave and poet utters this prayer: whoever chants to the Guru night and day,
Supplicates the slave minstrel, whosoever recites the Name of the Great Guru by day and night,
Whoever chants the True Guru's Name day and night with mind and speech: Sri Das Bhatt ji says in prayer:
NAJ3: Rid mahi = in the heart. Dharai = enshrines. Duhthe = from both. Rahai = is saved. ||3||7||
Whoever enshrines the True Guru's Name in the heart is saved from both birth and death. ||3||7||
whoever enshrines the Name of the Guru within his heart, is rid of both birth and death. ||3||7||
and enshrines the Guru's Name in his mind, he is rid of both birth and death.
O True Guru ji! Whoever holds your Name in the heart becomes free of both the pains of birth and death. ||3||7||
Q283: Ghor andhar = fearful darkness, pitch darkness.
Without (taking refuge with) the True Guru there is nothing but darkness (on the path of human life); without the Guru the understanding (of right living) cannot be gained.
Without the Guru, there is utter darkness; without the Guru, understanding does not come.
Without the Guru, there is pitch darkness and without the Guru, understanding is obtained not.
Without the True Guru there is fearful (ghor) darkness of ignorance for this being, and without the Guru it does not even come to understand its own true form.
CTZF: Without the Guru the attention does not become (lofty) and success (in the battle of life) is not gained either; without the Guru there is no release (from vices).
Without the Guru, there is no intuitive awareness or success; without the Guru, there is no liberation.
Without the Guru, man can obtain not divine comprehension and success, and, without the Guru, he is blessed not with emancipation.
Without the True Guru this being has no awareness (surat) of Vahiguru and gains no siddhi either; and without the Guru it does not attain liberation either.
1725: O my mind! Take refuge with the True Guru; this is the highest reflection.
So make Him your Guru, and contemplate the Truth; make Him your Guru, O my mind.
Come you into the Guru's fold, yea, my soul, come you into the Guru's fold for the true reflection of the Lord.
O my mind! Take up the Guru, through the Guru reflecting on the True Form.
DAE3: Sabad sapunn = sabad sampann, rich in the Word, a hero of the Word. Aghan = sins.
Take refuge with the Guru who is a hero of the Word; all your sins will be cut away.
Make Him your Guru, who is embellished and exalted in the Word of the Shabad; all your sins shall be washed away.
Adopt you the Guru, who is embellished with the Name, so that all your sins may be washed off.
Take as Guru one who is rich in the Word (sabad sapunn), meaning learned in scripture and established in Brahm, who will cut away all your sins.
PXM6: Nayan = in the eyes. Bayan = in speech. Karahu = enshrine. Sat = eternal.
The poet Nalya says (O my mind!) enshrine only the Guru in your eyes and in your speech; the Guru is eternal.
So speaks NALL the poet: with your eyes, make Him your Guru; with the words you speak, make Him your Guru, your True Guru.
Says Kall, the bard, by yours eyes and words contemplate you the Guru, the Great Guru, yea, the True Guru.
Sri 'Nal Bhatt' ji utters: O brother! The True Guru alone is the True Form; so see the True Guru with your eyes and always utter (his Name) with your speech.
6794: Keeau = took up. Akayab [sic: for 'akayath'] = fruitless. Te = those people. Jin = who (each person who). Nahu = not. Keeau = did, took up. ||4||8||
Each person who has not had the True Guru's vision, and each person who has not taken refuge with the True Guru, all of them (have come) into the world fruitlessly. ||4||8||
Those who have not seen the Guru, who have not made Him their Guru, are useless in this world. ||4||8||
They who have neither seen nor adopted the Guru, vain are they in this world.
The person who has not seen the True Guru's vision and has not accepted the teaching: such people are useless (akayab) in the world. ||4||8||
6EA8: Dwell upon the Guru, the Guru, the Guru, O my mind.
O my soul, you recite the Name of the Guru, the Guru, the Guru.
So, O my mind! Utter the True Guru's Name in all three times.

LUHE: Taran taran = a ship to carry across. Taran = ship. Samrath = able. Kalijug = in the Kaliyug. Sunat = on hearing. Sabad jis kere = whose Word (the Guru's). Kere = of. Samadh = samadhi (one becomes absorbed in).
The Guru, on hearing whose bani (one becomes absorbed) in samadhi, is in the Kaliyug a ship able to carry (one across the world-ocean).
The All-powerful Guru is the Boat to carry us across in this Dark Age of Kali Yuga. Hearing the Word of His Shabad, we are transported into Samaadhi.
In this darkage, the Omnipotent Guru is a ship to ferry across, hearing whose word, one lands in profound trance.
The True Guru is able, like a ship (taran), to carry one across the world-ocean; and in this Kaliyug, on hearing his Word, samadhi comes at once, meaning the mind's attention becomes one-pointed.
UGNS: Phun = and further. Dukhan nas = the destroyer of pains. Soorau = hero. Tih nere = near that person.
That Guru destroys pains, a hero who gives comforts. Whoever holds him in meditation, that Guru dwells with them.
He is the Spiritual Hero who destroys pain and brings peace. Whoever meditates on Him, dwells near Him.
He is such a hero, who destroys pain in an instant and can bestow peace. Whosoever contemplates him, near him he abides.
Further, the True Guru is a hero who destroys pains and gives comfort; and whoever holds his meditation, meaning he dwells near them, he dwells in the very hearts of his servants.
EQWA: Poorau = perfect. Ridai = in the heart. Mukh = (that Guru's) face. Agh = sins. Jahi parere = are driven away.
The True Guru is the perfect Being; the Guru remembers Hari in his heart; on seeing (his) face, sins are driven away.
He is the Perfect Primal Being, who meditates in remembrance on the Lord within his heart; seeing His Face, sins run away.
The Guru is the perfect person, who remembers Lord in the mind. Seeing the face of such a Guru, the sins are washed away.
The True Guru, the perfect Being, remembers Hari in his heart, and by seeing his lotus face all sins are driven far away (parere).
LZAL: Jau = if. Har budh = godly understanding. ||5||9||
O my mind! If you want godly understanding, riddhis and siddhis, then chant 'Guru, Guru'. ||5||9||
If you long for wisdom, wealth, spiritual perfection and properity, O my mind, dwell upon the Guru, the Guru, the Guru. ||5||9||
O my mind, if you desire Godly wisdom, wealth and prosperity; then contemplate on that Guru who is the Guru of the Gurus.
O my mind! If you want understanding (har budh) that knows the self, and riddhis and siddhis, then utter the Guru ji's Name with mind, speech and body. ||5||9||
R8H5: Guru mukh = the True Guru's face. Garoo sukh = great joy. Garoo = (gariyas, the comparative of guru, 'heavy, great'). Payau = has found, has taken.
On seeing the True Guru's (Amardas ji's) face, (Guru Ramdas ji) has found great joy.
Gazing upon the Face of the Guru, I find peace.
Seeing the Guru's face, I have obtained perfect peace.
O True Guru ji! On seeing your face I have found great (garoo) joy.
CUFN: Hutee ju pias = the thirst that (there) was. Pioos = amrit (piyush). Pivann kee = of drinking. Banchhat = longed for [sic: printed 'man-izzat', likely 'man-ichhat']. Kau = for. Bidh = the means. Milayau = has brought together, has arranged.
The longing that (he) had to drink amrit: (Hari) has arranged the means of fulfilling that heartfelt (longing).
I was thirsty, yearning to drink in the Nectar; to fulfill that wish, the Guru laid out the way.
I had the thirst to in-drink the Nectar. For fulfilling that aspiration, the Lord has chalked out a way.
The thirst I had to drink the amrit (pioos) of teaching: for the fulfilment of my heart's longing, the Creator (bidh) has brought me to you.
3RJH: Bho = has become. Thaur baso = has settled in its place, has come to rest. Ras basan siu = with tastes and desires. Ju = the mind which. Dahan dis = in the ten directions. Dhayau = runs.
That mind which (in worldly beings) runs in the ten directions after tastes and desires: his mind has been satisfied and has come to rest.
My mind has become perfect; it dwells in the Lord's Place; it had been wandering in all directions, in its desire for tastes and pleasures.
My mind, which wandered in ten directions stung with the desire of relish has become perfect and now abides in the Lord's abode.

My mind, which used to run in all ten directions with desires for the pleasures (ras) of the senses, has now, through your teaching, become full and settled in its place, meaning in the all-pervading Brahm.
BY65: Gobind puree sam = like the city of Hari, like heaven. Sam = equal, like. Jalyan teer Bipas = on the bank of the waters of the Beas.
(The True Guru Amardas ji, who) has built Goindval, like heaven, on the bank of the waters of the Beas,
Goindwal is the City of God, built on the bank of the Beas River.
Says Jallan, Goindwal built on the bank of river Beas is like the city of the Lord.
Sri 'Jalan' Bhatt ji says: Guru Amardas ji, who built the city of Gobind, like heaven, on the bank of the Beas river.
0N1M: Barkhan ko dukh = the pain of years. Teer = on the bank. ||6||10||
On seeing that Guru's face (Guru Ramdas ji) has found great joy; (his, as it were) pain of years has gone away. ||6||10||
The pains of so many years have been taken away; gazing upon the Face of the Guru, I find peace. ||6||10||
Seeing the vision of the Guru, my grief of many years has been dispelled far away and I have obtained great peace.
The pain born of ignorance that lasted many years has now gone, because, O True Guru, on seeing his lotus face I have found great (garoo) joy, meaning the joy of the self. ||6||10||
C5J4: The all-powerful Guru (Amardas ji) has placed his hand on (Guru Ramdas ji's) head.
The All-powerful Guru placed His hand upon my head.
The all mighty Guru has placed his hand upon my head.
Such an all-powerful Satgur Amardas ji has placed his hand on the head of Sri Guru Ramdas ji.
AF60: Gur = the True Guru. Jis dekh charann = on seeing whose (the Guru's) feet. Aghann = sins. Haryau = went away.
On seeing whose (Guru Amardas ji's) feet sins go away, that Guru has shown grace and blessed (Guru Ramdas ji) with Hari's Name;
The Guru was kind, and blessed me with the Lord's Name. Gazing upon His Feet, my sins were dispelled.
The Guru has shown mercy and has blessed me with the Lord's Name. Seeing the Lord's feet, my sins are washed off.
He who in his grace has given all the Sikhs the teaching of Hari's Name, by seeing whose lotus feet the Sikhs have taken away, that is, removed, their sins (aghann).
90NJ: Nis basur = night and day. Basur = day. Ek saman = steady, unchanging. Sut bhan = the son of the sun, Yama. Bhan = the sun. Sune = suni, on hearing.
(Guru Ramdas ji's) meditation (on that Name) stays steady night and day; on hearing that Name even Yama, the king of death, is afraid (that is, does not come near).
Night and day, the Guru meditates on the One Lord; hearing His Name, the Messenger of Death is scared away.
Night and day, the Guru incessantly contemplates the Lord and hearing his Name 'Yama', the son of the sun, is scared.

He who day and night keeps his meditation steadily on Sri Akal Purakh. And on merely hearing the name of Sri Guru Amardas Sahib ji, even Dharamraja, the son of the sun, was afraid; meaning, while the third Patshah ji was at Goindval ji, no son died while his parents were living.
5H4L: Bhan = say. Das = O servant (the poet Nalya)! Jagatr guru = the Guru of the world. Paras bhet = on meeting the philosopher's stone (Guru Amardas ji). Paras = worthy of being touched (a philosopher's stone). Karyau = has been made.

O servant (poet Nalya)! Guru Ramdas ji has hope only in the Guru of the world; on meeting the philosopher's stone (Guru Amardas ji), he too has become worthy of being touched (a philosopher's stone himself).
So speaks the Lord's slave: Guru Raam Daas placed His Faith in Guru Amar Daas, the Guru of the World; touching the Philosopher's Stone, He was transformed into the Philosopher's Stone.
Says the Guru's slave that the Guru (Ram Dass) leaned on the world-teacher, Guru Amar Dass, who uniting him with the philosopher's stone, has made him the philosopher's stone.
Sri Das Bhatt ji says: I have hope in that Guru of the world, Satguru Amardas ji, the philosopher's stone, who, uniting him with himself, has made him a philosopher's stone too.
0F6X: Hari has made Guru Ramdas ji unshakable, (because) the all-powerful Guru (Amardas ji) has placed his hand on (his) head. ||7||11||
Guru Raam Daas recognized the Lord as True; the All-powerful Guru placed His hand upon His head. ||7||11||
When the All-powerful Guru placed his hand on the head of Guru Ram Dass, then he realised the Lord as True.
When the all-powerful Satguru Amardas Sahib ji placed his hand on his head, then Sri Guru Ramdas Sahib ji went on to know Hari for certain (sat). ||7||11||
XV6S: (O True Guru ji!) Now save the honour of this servant (Nalya) the Bhatt,
Now, please preserve the honor of Your humble slave.
O my Guru, now save you the honour of Dass, your bard.
He prays: O True Guru ji! I am the Bhatt named Das; now save my honour in the same way.
BUPG: Phare = tore apart. Kar = hand. Kar aj = with the nails of the hands.
As (you) saved the honour of the devotee Prahlad and killed Harnakhash with the nails of your hands.
God saved the honor of the devotee Prahlaad, when Harnaakhash tore him apart with his claws.
As God saved the honour of saint Prahlad by tearing Harnakhash with His hand nails.
Just as you saved the honour of your devotee Prahlad ji by tearing open Harnakhash's belly with the nails (aj) of your hand (kar).
V2XJ: Chheenat = while being snatched away. Deen = gave. Saj = supplies.
And, O Lord Hari ji! You saved Draupadi's honour too; when her clothes were being snatched away, (you) then gave her plenty.
And the Dear Lord God saved the honor of Dropadi; when her clothes were stripped from her, she was blessed with even more.
And, as the Sire God Lord preserved the honour of Dropadi, by blessing her with good many more robes, when she was divested of her clothes.

And, O True Guru ji, Lord in the form of Hari! Seeing Draupadi about to be stripped naked by her clothes being snatched away by wicked men such as Shakuni and Duhshasan, you provided many garments, and so you saved her honour.
8JZ0: Apda = calamity, hardship. Rakhia = saved. Ganika = a prostitute. Poore = fulfilled, accomplished. Tih kaj = her (Ganika's) affairs.
O True Guru ji! You saved Sudama from calamity, and accomplished the affairs of Ganika as she recited (the Name of Ram).
Sudaamaa was saved from misfortune; and Ganikaa the prostitute - when she chanted Your Name, her affairs were perfectly resolved.
As, Sodama was saved from calamity and the courtesan recited the Lord's Name and He fulfilled her affairs,
Just as you saved the devotee Sudama from calamity, and the prostitute (Ganika), who recited only the Name in order to teach it to her parrot: so you fulfilled her affairs, such as liberation.
8M6Q: Satgur = O True Guru! Suprasann hoi = being pleased. Laj = honour, good name. ||8||12||
Now, in the time of the Kaliyug, be pleased with this servant (Nalya) the Bhatt (too) and save his honour. ||8||12||
O Great True Guru, if it pleases You, please save the honor of Your slave in this Dark Age of kali Yuga. ||8||12||
O Sire True Guru, becoming mighty pleased, similarly save you the honour of Dass, the Bard, in this Dark-age.
O Sri Satguru Ramdas Sahib ji! In the same way, be well pleased with me now and save the honour of me, the servant Bhatt, in this Kaliyug. ||8||12||
5CQ9: The name of this metre is jholna.
YJXJ: Chant Guru, Guru, Guru, Guru, Guru, O mortal beings.
O mortals, recite you the Name of your Guru, the great Guru, yea, the sublime Guru.
O breathing human beings! Chant 'Guru, Guru' at all times with mind, body and speech.
UG68: Apai = arpai, offers. Rasan = with the tongue. Ahinis = day and night (that is, at all times). Rasai = enjoys, remembers. Sat kar = as true, as right. Janeeahu = know, understand.
Know (this) as true: that (the True Guru himself) chants Hari's Word, gives (others) the nine treasures of the Name, and at all times enjoys (the Name) with his tongue.
Chant the Shabad, the Word of the Lord, Har, Har; the Naam, the Name of the Lord, brings the nine treasures. With your tongue, taste it, day and night, and know it as true.
Know you this as true, that the Guru recites the Lord God's Name, blesses others with the Name's nine treasures and his tongue day and night tastes the Name.

The True Guru chants the Word 'Har Har' and offers (apai) the Sikhs the Name, which is the nine treasures; and with his tongue he stays absorbed (rasai) in that Vahiguru day and night. So, O brother, know this as true.
EG0N: Prem rang = the dye of love. Gurmukhahi = facing the Guru. Ann marag = other paths, other sects. Tajahu = abandon. Gyaneeahu = O wise friends!
(If) we remember (Hari) taking the Guru's teaching, then the colour of Hari's love is gained; (so) O wise ones! Abandon other paths and remember Hari.
Then, you shall obtain His Love and Affection; become Gurmukh, and meditate on Him. Give up all other ways; vibrate and meditate on Him, O spiritual people.
Again, O divines, be blessed with the Lord's love and affection and, abandoning other ways, remember and contemplate your God, through the supreme Guru.

In that True Guru, bliss (rang) is gained through love; so let us meditate on Vahiguru through that True Guru. O wise and understanding people! Abandon other paths and remember only Hari's Name through the Guru; or, remember Hari through the wise.
CN8U: Rid = in the heart. Bachan gur = the True Guru's words. Panch bhoo = the mind. Bas karahu = bring under control. Udharahu = carry across, make fruitful. Dvar har = at Hari's door, in Hari's court. Maneeahu = you will be honoured.
(O people!) Enshrine the True Guru's words in your heart (and in this way) bring your mind under control; make your birth and family fruitful; you will be honoured at Hari's door.
Enshrine the Word of the Guru's Teachings within your heart, and overpower the five passions. Your life, and your generations, shall be saved, and you shall be honored at the Lord's Door.
Enshrine the Lord's Name in your mind, overwhelm your heart of five elements and save your life and lineage. This wise you shall be honoured in the Lord's Court.

Hold the words of that True Guru in your heart; and when you bring the five demon-vices, lust, anger and the rest, under control, you will also deliver your families. And, fulfilled in this very birth, you will be honoured at Hari's door, the congregation of the true, or in the next world; meaning, you will have honour.
TA3H: Jaut = if. It ut = of here and there, of this world and the next. Sabh sukh banchhvahu = you want all comforts. ||1||13||
If you want all the comforts of this world and the next, then, O people, always chant 'Guru, Guru'. ||1||13||
If you desire all the peace and comforts of this world and the next, then chant Guru, Guru, Guru, Guru, Guru, O mortal beings. ||1||13||
If you desire all the comforts of this and that world, O mortal, then recite you, the Name of your Guru, the great Guru, the sublime Guru.
If (jau t) you want comfort in this world and the next, then, O people, utter only the Guru ji's Name with mind, body and speech. ||1||13||
05GV: O saints! O Sikhs of the Guru! Chant 'Guru, Guru' with faith.
Chant Guru, Guru, Guru, Guru, Guru, and know Him as true.
Deeming Him as True, O man, meditate you on your God, the great Teacher, yea, the Teacher of the teachers.
Chant the Guru at all times with mind and speech, with certainty (sat).
NTWV: Agam gun nidhan = the treasure of infinite virtues. Jan = the knower. Man = in the mind. Dhar = holding.
Enshrining the True Guru's words in your heart, enshrine in your mind Hari, the knower (of every heart) and the treasure of infinite virtues, and meditate on him day and night.
Know that the Lord is the Treasure of Excellence. Enshrine Him in your mind, and meditate on Him. Enshrine the Word of the Guru's Teachings within your heart.
Know you that God is the infinite treasure of virtues. So contemplate Him in the mind and, day and night. rcite and enshrine the Guru's word in your heart.
Holding the True Guru's words in your heart, know the True Guru to be Hari, the unreachable treasure (nidhan) of virtues, and hold his meditation in your mind night and day.
HURJ: Bimal = pure. Athah = deep. Majan = bathing. Gursikh = O Sikhs of the Guru! Rang sar = in the pool of love. Tarahu = swim.
O saints! O Sikhs of the Guru! Then dive into the pure and deep water of the True Guru, and swim in the pool of love for the True Name.
Then, cleanse yourself in the Immaculate and Unfathomable Water of the Guru; O Gursikhs and Saints, cross over the Ocean of Love of the True Name.
Then take you bath in the Guru's immaculate and unfathomable water and swim about in the love-ocean of the True Name, O saints and Guru's disciples.
O Sikhs of the Guru ji! The True Guru, the form of peace, is the fathomless pool of the pure water of the True Name; when you bathe in it with love (rang), you will cross the world-ocean.
N1U6: Japai = (the Guru who) chants. Ras = in the joy. Bhagat har = devotion to Hari.
(Guru Ramdas, who) always chants the Formless One, free of enmity and fear, and in the joy of love for the True Guru's Word makes devotion to Hari firm,
Meditate lovingly forever on the Lord, free of hate and vengeance, Formless and Fearless; lovingly savor the Word of the Guru's Shabad, and implant devotional worship of the Lord deep within.
The Guru ever lovingly meditates on the Envy-free, Formless and Fear-free Lord and with relish grasps God's Name and devotion.
The True Guru, always free of enmity, fearlessly chants the Formless One, and through love of the Guru's teaching (sabad) makes the taste of devotion to Hari firm in the heart.
3C0J: Mugadh man = O foolish mind! Gurmukh = through the Guru. ||2||14||
Facing that Guru, O foolish mind, chant (Hari's) Name and give up doubt; say 'Guru, Guru' with faith. ||2||14||
O foolish mind, give up your doubts; as Gurmukh, vibrate and meditate on the Naam. Chant Guru, Guru, Guru, Guru, Guru, and know Him as true. ||2||14||
O my foolish mind, discard your doubt and recite the Name by the Guru's grace, Deeming Him as true, meditate you on your God, the great Teacher, the Teacher of the teacher.
O foolish mind! Give up doubt, remember the Name through that Guru, and with certainty remember 'Guru, Guru' with mind, body and speech. ||2||14||
